question.problem:
Consider the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ and the vector $b,$ given by

$$
A={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}-4 & -6 \\ 0 & -3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U},\,b=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -6\end{aligned}].
$$

If $⟨{x}_{1},{x}_{2}⟩$ and $⟨{y}_{1},{y}_{2}⟩$ are the solutions to the systems $Ax=b$ and $Ly=b$ respectively, what is the value of ${y}_{1}+3{x}_{2}?$

current_example.problem:
Consider the LU decomposition of the matrix $A$ and the vector $\mathbf{b},$ given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156398/assets/d3538562aaba72979df662b2d96e668a2b666fd716490fa7516fa360507c2e95.svg)
If $\langle x_1,x_2 \rangle$ and $\langle y_1,y_2 \rangle$ are the solutions to the systems $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}$ and $L\mathbf{y}=\mathbf{b}$ respectively, what is the value of $x_1 \cdot y_2?$
current_example.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y},$ we obtain

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156398/assets/dd3b2fec18439c7b5c7a5f610ab62c1890a1bace4c17d5f64941087bd20abf29.svg)

Now, we solve the two systems in turn.

- First, we solve $L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156398/assets/269bb926dc540d8ae46889721b5bea2854fa8090717536d1eaab5d2de682c3c2.svg)
This gives the system of equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=6 \\ -2{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=-8.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is $y_1=6$ and $y_2=4.$ Therefore, 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156398/assets/60e5b8c93385ee2628ec3ce7adf8eacd5cc774287b3e8cedffdf65f1016c3a15.svg)

- Next, we solve $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156398/assets/0daaedefcc074f3eb93bb9dd7ed9e0c2e8532acd32a76fc2fc920d4a6f0c8d1e.svg)
This gives the system of equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}7{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=6 \\ -2{x}_{2}=4.\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this system is $x_2=-2$ and $x_1=2.$ Therefore, 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14156398/assets/c1fff3f0159eb48d3cc346b5ec672e58dab3216720f0a11f87e1d809d1cfeddc.svg)

Finally, $x_1 \cdot y_2 = 2 \cdot 4 = 8.$
